page: Amazon Web Services m5.metal is a bare-metal, general-purpose server configuration powered by dual Intel Xeon 8259CL processors running at 3.1 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs with dedicated CPU allocation and hyperthreading enabled. The system includes 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced ratio of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Direct physical access without hypervisor intervention exposes hardware virtualization extensions (VMX) and vector instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI support.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput across high-concurrency workloads. The server achieves top-quartile performance in multi-core compute tests, including a PassMark CPU score of 57,076.55 and a stress-ng multi-core score of 81,982.12. In-memory operations show high bandwidth, recording 218.48 GB/sec in large uncached reads and 76.75 million Redis SET operations per second. Clang compilation and ray tracing benchmarks also fall within the top 25%. In contrast, single-thread metrics such as Geekbench single-core (1329.0) and single-core stress-ng (1457.1) sit in the median distribution. Large language model text generation performance is low, reflecting the absence of specialized accelerators.

The hardware configuration includes 25 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without local attached storage or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached storage. From a cost-efficiency perspective, m5.metal offers high resource density by packing 96 hardware threads and extensive memory bandwidth onto a single non-virtualized node, reducing licensing and hypervisor overhead for large-scale enterprise deployments.

Amazon Web Services m5.metal is well-suited for high-throughput transactional databases, large-scale multi-threaded compiling, enterprise caching tiers, microservices container consolidation, and bare-metal hypervisor hosting.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.metal is a bare-metal general-purpose instance powered by Intel Xeon 8259CL processors, delivering 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs at 3.1 GHz without hypervisor overhead. Equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR4 memory across a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU distribution, the server provides top-quartile multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth, reaching 218.48 GB/sec in large read operations and 76.75 million Redis SET operations per second. Networking is anchored by a 25 Gbps baseline interface, while persistent storage must be connected over the network due to the lack of bundled local drives. With hardware support for AVX-512 and direct virtualization access, m5.metal provides high resource density for parallel tasks, although per-core single-threaded output remains mid-tier. The platform is engineered for high-concurrency database workloads, software compilation, memory-intensive caching clusters, and custom virtualization stacks requiring direct access to bare-metal resources.
